attachments.text:
ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-07-15
Provider: Dr. Raj Patel, MD
Department: Pediatrics
Visit Type: inpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Sudden onset of weakness and abdominal pain

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
Patient is a 6-year-old male with sickle cell disease (HbSS), chronic hemolytic anemia, and dactylitis in infancy who presented previously with abdominal pain. He presents to the emergency department with his mother, who reports he has been experiencing sudden onset of weakness and abdominal pain since this morning. Mother also notes he has seemed unusually pale and has been less active than usual.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Sickle cell disease with vaso-occlusive crisis (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Sickle cell disease (HbSS genotype)
- Chronic hemolytic anemia
- History of dactylitis in infancy

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- None

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Penicillin V potassium 250 mg orally twice daily
- Folic acid 1 mg orally daily
- Hydroxyurea 600 mg orally once daily (weight-based dosing)

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Father - sickle cell trait (HbAS)
- Mother - sickle cell trait (HbAS)
- Maternal uncle - sickle cell disease
- Neonatal screening positive for sickle cell disease at birth

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: Never. Occupation: Elementary school student (1st grade).

VITAL SIGNS:
His temperature is 37.2°C (99°F), blood pressure is 90/60 mmHg, pulse is 130/min, and respiratory rate is 22/min.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On examination, the child appears lethargic and is noted to have pallor. Abdominal examination reveals a palpable mass on the left side below the costal margin, consistent with splenomegaly.

LABORATORY DATA:
Laboratory tests are ordered, and the results are as follows:
- Hemoglobin: 6 g/dL (Normal: 11-15.5 g/dL)
- Hematocrit: 18% (Normal: 34-45%)
- Platelet count: 250,000/mm³ (Normal: 150,000-450,000/mm³)
- White blood cell count: 12,000/mm³ (Normal: 4,500-11,000/mm³)
- Reticulocyte count: 10% (Normal: 0.5-2.5%)
- Peripheral blood smear: Sickled erythrocytes

attachments.text:
ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-01-15
Provider: Dr. Sarah Johnson, MD
Department: Emergency Medicine
Visit Type: ed

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Severe abdominal pain

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
His parents report that he has had intermittent pain episodes in his hands and feet since infancy. Today he developed sharp pain in the right lower quadrant along with fatigue and mild yellowing of the eyes. There is no history of recent travel or sick contacts.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Sickle cell disease (HbSS genotype)
- Chronic hemolytic anemia
- History of dactylitis in infancy

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- None

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Penicillin V potassium 250 mg orally twice daily
- Folic acid 1 mg orally daily
- Hydroxyurea 600 mg orally once daily (weight-based dosing)

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Father - sickle cell trait (HbAS)
- Mother - sickle cell trait (HbAS)
- Maternal uncle - sickle cell disease
- Neonatal screening positive for sickle cell disease at birth

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: Never. Occupation: Elementary school student (1st grade).

VITAL SIGNS:
His temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), blood pressure is 102/68 mmHg, pulse is 108/min, and respirations are 20/min.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On examination, there is tenderness in the right lower abdomen without guarding or rebound. Scleral icterus is noted.

LABORATORY DATA:
Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 7.9 g/dL
Mean corpuscular volume 85 fL
Reticulocyte count 9%
Total bilirubin 3.1 mg/dL (mostly indirect)
